subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the person who killed the victim is the one who took the heart, because everything else is just people talking and the heart is a fact.
source_quote: "Right, but at the end of the day, I'm pretty sure that the person that killed him is the one that took the heart," I said. Everything else is people talking. The heart is a fact.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wants to know if the High Tower has been compromised and whether Kalan himself might have used the key to enter it.
source_quote: Thorin wanted to know if it had been compromised — whether Kalan himself might have used the key, walked in, walked out.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin does not argue when Kalan calls the investigators outsiders who were hired to bungle the case.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, didn't argue the insult. "I don't doubt that maybe they hired us because they thought we were gonna screw it up."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan chose Grygum to receive the key deliberately, not by chance.
source_quote: The key went to Grygum. I marked that before anything else — not into Daz's hand, not into Thorin's, not into the open air for whoever was closest. Kalan stepped out of a doorway we hadn't clocked... He chose the orc. I don't think it was chance.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir tells Kalan they are only there because someone put them up to it and they are happy to not get involved — and believes this to be true.
source_quote: "Purely accidental," I told him. "We have no particular involvement here. Someone put us up to this. We are happy to not get involved." True enough. Filed under things that are also true.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes Kalan was hasty in assuming the murderer was the one who rifled the safe, and corrects him by pointing out the key was in the locket.
source_quote: I stopped him. The key was in the locket. The locket was around the keeper's neck. The locket was gone. So why would the killer go through the safe at all?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects Kalan is being set up to fail and that the real凶手 is being protected by Bookwyrm or someone else.
source_quote: He suspected, he said, was that one of the Great Readers was the murderer, and that either Bookwyrm was protecting them or someone had convinced her to fire him to protect themselves.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks Kalan is at risk of being killed over a key he no longer has and warns him to watch his back because shapeshifters exist.
source_quote: "Given that you're at risk of being killed over a key you don't have anymore, watch your back," I told him. "Keep in mind there are people who can change their form. Shapeshift. Whatever you want to call it."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes Kalan is a good investigator who is being deliberately sidelined and that his own team has already outperformed him.
source_quote: "Is he aware that someone was pretending to be Sylvira Savikas the night of the murder?" He went still. "No. That is new information." A pause. "You are very good at this."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum remembers that midnight tears poison only takes effect at midnight, matching the time of death.
source_quote: The creature that ingests this poison suffers no effect until the stroke of midnight. "That is a good match for, for the... what actually happened," I said. "He died at roughly midnight."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes the poison was delivered via the book because the victim licked his fingers while reading, causing the poison to react with saliva and darken.
source_quote: Some liquid had gotten onto his finger, and the finger had gone black. Thorin asked the right thing — was the black the poison going dark as it took hold? No. The dust stays pale ochre. What darkens it is saliva. The ochre reacts on contact with spit, and a man turning pages licks his fingers to do it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understands the sapphire summoning spell allows a person to recall a hidden object to their hand, even if it was thrown away.
source_quote: Oh, I see," I said, "so you can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever. Nobody will find it, and then when you need it back, boom.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum knows the sapphire summoning spell does not work on items worn on the body, which reframes how the key might have been hidden.
source_quote: It doesn't, as it turned out. Which reframed the whole use. "Oh, I see," I said, "so you can put it someplace, you can throw it into a river or whatever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum finds the book *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi* by Archibald Roots, Jr., and feels it was almost as if the book leaned into his hand.
source_quote: And then I found it faster than I had any right to. The right book practically leaned into my hand — a volume titled *Fey-mous Flowers & Fungi*, by one Archibald Roots, Jr., son of the legendary gnome botanist Archibald Roots Sr. I almost laughed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feels a sense of peace and focus in the library, contrasting with his past underground experiences.
source_quote: It is a strange thing, after months underground, to research in a room with shelves taller than the ceilings I'd learned to stoop beneath. No Faerzress humming behind my eyes. No tunnel that might put an enemy in front of me by the time I turned a page. Just stacks, and quiet, and the work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thinks the summoning spell described by Grygum could be used to teleport the High Tower key into the holder’s hand, but then realizes it doesn't work on worn items.
source_quote: I heard Daz say it in my head - "Oh, wait a second, this is like a way to teleport it into my hand later kind of thing."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices that Daral Yashenti is setting the venue to the Hearth to maintain control and continue drinking where he’s comfortable.
source_quote: Fembris went off with the particular efficiency of someone who'd been waiting for a task to belong to, and came back with two words. Daral was not coming to us. We were to go to the Hearth. I noted the inversion before we'd even left the room — the suspect setting the venue, picking the ground, making the famous detectives walk to him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refuses to accept the label 'Bookwyrm's brownnosers' that Daral Yashenti gives them.
source_quote: "Oh, look, it's Faerûn's most famous detectives! Bookwyrm's brownnosers, I'm going to call you, because you like to—" "That's not our," Grygum said, "that's not our chosen name."
